name: Carshena
overview: Carshena is a male figure identified as one of the seven princes of Persia and Media, a notable position of authority within the biblical context. Scripture does not provide information about his tribe or additional personal details. His role as a prince highlights his significance in the governance or spiritual oversight related to these regions.
namesAndTitles: The name Carshena appears in Scripture also as Cashena, which possibly means 'black.' This proper name does not have a direct divine attribution but serves to identify him uniquely among the princes mentioned.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Carshena beyond his designation as one of the seven princes of Persia and Media. There are no listed relatives or descendants associated with him in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Carshena's importance lies in his role as one of the seven princes who held authority over Persia and Media, indicating a position of spiritual or governmental influence. His mention in the biblical narrative underscores the existence of divine or angelic beings assigned to oversee nations, reflecting God's sovereign control over earthly realms. Although details are limited, his inclusion points to the broader theme of God's governance through appointed princes.
